;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[Taliban insurgency]]
***[[October 2020 Afghanistan attacks]]
****The [[Taliban]] kills four Afghan [[Afghan Armed Forces|soldier]]s and four [[Afghan National Police|police]] officers in [[Aliabad District]], [[Kunduz Province]]. Five soldiers and two police are also injured in the attack. In [[Helmand Province]], the Taliban kills at least three security forces and injures another three. [https://tolonews.com/afghanistan-166919 (TOLOnews)]
*[[Second Nagorno-Karabakh War]]
**[[Armenia]] and [[Azerbaijan]] agree to a [[ceasefire]] in the disputed [[Nagorno-Karabakh]] effective 03:00 a.m. local time, following [[Russia]]n-brokered peace talks in [[Moscow]]. However, fighting continues and both sides accuse each other of violating the agreement. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-54488386 (BBC News)]
*[[Mali War]]
**[[Switzerland]] says it has been informed that a female [[Swiss people|Swiss]] [[hostage]] has been killed in [[Mali]] by [[jihadist]] group [[Jama'at Nasr al-Islam wal Muslimin]]. The exact circumstances of the killing are still unclear, according to [[Federal Department of Foreign Affairs|Foreign Minister]] [[Ignazio Cassis]]. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-swiss-mali/swiss-hostage-in-mali-killed-swiss-foreign-ministry-idUKKBN26U2FD?il=0 (Reuters)]
*An attack leaves at least eight people dead at a camp for [[Rohingya people]] in [[Bangladesh]]. Bangladeshi authorities detain 12 people after multiple attacks, including arson and gunfire, occurred for several days. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/10/9/several-killed-in-gang-war-at-rohingya-camps-in-bangladesh (Al Jazeera English)]

;Arts and culture
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the performing arts]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in New York City]]
**[[The Broadway League]] announces that the [[Broadway theatre|Broadway theaters]] will remain closed through May 2021. [https://www.cnbc.com/2020/10/09/broadway-to-remain-closed-through-may-30.html (CNBC)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2020 Atlantic hurricane season]]
**[[Hurricane Delta]]
***Hurricane Delta makes landfall in the [[U.S. state]] of [[Louisiana]]. During its time in Louisiana, it downgraded to a Category 2 Hurricane. [https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/hurricane-delta-2020-10-08/ (CBS News)]
*An explosion kills at least four people in [[Beirut]], [[Lebanon]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-lebanon-crisis-fire/four-dead-several-injured-in-beirut-fuel-tank-explosion-idUSKBN26U2II (Reuters)]
*Eighty-eight people are injured following an apartment fire in [[Ulsan]], [[South Korea]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/amp/International/wireStory/fire-south-korean-apartment-high-rise-hurts-88-73512770 (ABC News)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Community of Madrid]]
*****The [[Government of Spain|national government]] imposes a 15-day [[state of emergency]] in [[Madrid]] and nine surrounding cities in an attempt to bring down [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] infection rates in the capital, after a court yesterday overturned a partial lockdown imposed last week. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-54478320 (BBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****The reported number of new infections in [[France]] jumped by 20,339, a new record since the beginning of the pandemic, making the cumulative total at 691,977, according to data from the [[Minister of Health (France)|health ministry]] website. [https://www.france24.com/en/20201009-french-covid-19-cases-climb-by-more-than-20-000-in-a-single-day-in-new-record (France 24)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****[[Chancellor of Germany|Chancellor]] [[Angela Merkel]] and mayors of 11 large cities agrees on stricter controls for urban areas exceeding the government COVID-19 threshold. She said for cities with more than 50 cases per 100,000 inhabitants over a seven-day period, which [[Berlin]] and [[Frankfurt]] already exceed that number, tighter restrictions should be implemented immediately. [https://www.dw.com/en/coronavirus-merkel-and-mayors-agree-on-tougher-restrictions/a-55215422 (DW)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****[[Italy]] registers 5,372 new cases in the past 24 hours, which it is the first time that the country reports more than 5,000 cases since late-March, prompting fears of second wave of COVID-19 that happens in other countries in Europe. [https://amp.rte.ie/amp/1170554/ (RTÉ)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]]
****[[Portugal]] reports 1,394 new daily cases, bringing the cumulative totals to 83,928 confirmed cases and 2,062 [[COVID-19 pandemic deaths|deaths]]. Ever since the end of national [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] in May, this has been the ninth time that the country has registered some record increases in new cases, with all other eight records occurring since the beginning of September. [https://covid19.min-saude.pt/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/221_DGS_boletim_20201009.pdf (DGS)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports 12,126 new cases, bringing the total number of cases to 1.27 million, according to data from health authorities. This sets a new record for daily infections surpassing the previous record on May 11, when 11,656 new cases were reported. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/latest-on-coronavirus-outbreak/russia-sees-highest-daily-rise-in-virus-cases/2001034 (Anadolu Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Switzerland]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Liechtenstein]]
****The number of new cases in [[Switzerland]] and [[Liechtenstein]] increases by 1,487 in a single day, a record since the beginning of the outbreak, according to data from Switzerland's [[Federal Office of Public Health]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-swiss-cases-idUSKBN26U11V (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Northern Ireland]]
*****[[Northern Ireland]] reports 1,080 new cases in the last 24 hours, which become the highest daily total for the number of positive tests since the [[Department of Health (Northern Ireland)|Department of Health]] rolled out its current testing model. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/amp/uk-northern-ireland-54174876 (BBC News)]
***[[Europe]] reports 100,000 daily COVID-19 cases for the first time since the outbreak. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-health-coronavirus-europe-cases-graph/europe-records-100000-daily-coronavirus-cases-for-first-time-idUKKBN26U1PS (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Nepal]]
****[[Nepal]] surpass 100,000 cases of [[COVID-19]]. [https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/south-asia/nepals-covid-19-cases-cross-100000-mark/articleshow/78575240.cms (''Times of India'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oman]]
****It is announced that [[Oman]] will reintroduce a night-time ban on movement and enforce the overnight closure of shops and public places between October 11 and 24, in an attempt to reduce the spread of COVID-19. This new curfew will apply from 8:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. local time, and Oman's beaches will also be closed until further notice. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/1746421/middle-east (''Arab News'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Uzbekistan]]
****The number of cases in [[Uzbekistan]] exceeds 60,000. [https://en.trend.az/casia/uzbekistan/3313380.html (Trend News Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ontario]]
****The [[government of Ontario|government]] announces that bars, indoor dining, gyms, and theatres in [[Toronto]], [[Ottawa]], and [[Regional Municipality of Peel|Peel Region]] will close due to a rise in cases. This comes after the province recorded 939 cases. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/toronto/covid-19-ontario-cases-friday-1.5756516 (CBC News)]
**The number of confirmed cases worldwide increased over 350,000, sets a new record since the beginning of the outbreak in [[China]], according to [[World Health Organization]]. [https://www.voanews.com/covid-19-pandemic/who-world-sets-one-day-record-over-350000-new-coronavirus-cases (Voice of America)]
;International relations
*[[Iran–United States relations]]
**In an expletive-laden interview on ''[[The Rush Limbaugh Show]]'', [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] warns [[Iran]], "not to fuck around" with the United States, and "if you do something bad to us, we are gonna do things to you that have never been done before". [https://thehill.com/policy/defense/520424-trump-warns-iran-dont-f-around-with-us (''The Hill'')]

;Law and crime
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on religion]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state)|COVID-19 pandemic in New York]]
***A federal judge refuses to block [[New York (state)|New York]] governor [[Andrew Cuomo]]'s plan to temporarily limit the size of religious gatherings in the virus hot spots. The district judge Kiyo Matsumoto issues the ruling after an emergency hearing in a lawsuit brought by [[rabbi]]s and [[synagogue]]s arguing that the restrictions were unconstitutional. [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/10/09/nyregion/cuomo-synagogues.html (''The New York Times'')]
*[[United States racial unrest (2020–2023)|2United States racial unrest]]
**[[Shooting of Alvin Cole]]
***Police in Wauwatosa announces that tear gas has been deployed as protests against the killing of Alvin Cole has occurred for three consecutive days. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/10/10/us/wauwatosa-wisconsin-alvin-cole-protests-saturday/index.html (CNN)] 
*[[Cannabis in the United States]]
**[[Cannabis in Vermont]]
***[[Vermont]] will become the 11th state to legalize marijuana for recreational use after [[Governor of Vermont|Governor]] [[Phil Scott]] said that he wouldn't veto a law passed by the [[Vermont General Assembly|state legislature]]. [https://thehill.com/homenews/state-watch/520373-vermont-to-legalize-recreational-marijuana (''The Hill'')]
*[[2020 California wildfires]]
**Equipment from the [[Pacific Gas and Electric Company]] are seized as part of an ongoing investigation into the company’s role in the [[Zogg Fire]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-pg-e-us-cal-fire/california-fire-department-confiscates-pges-equipment-in-wildfire-investigation-idUSKBN26U2MR (Reuters)]
*[[Omnibus Law on Job Creation]], [[Indonesia omnibus bill protests]]
**[[President of Indonesia|President]] [[Joko Widodo]] speaks about the controversy of [[Omnibus Law on Job Creation]], which triggered demonstrations and riots in various regions across the country. Jokowi claims the demonstration against the Job Creation Law was motivated by "disinformation regarding the substance of this law and hoaxes on social media". [https://news.detik.com/berita/d-5207352/jokowi-jawab-hoax-soal-uu-ciptaker-dari-ump-cuti-hingga-phk (detikNews)]
*[[Crime in Nigeria]]; [[Capital punishment in Nigeria]]
**[[Gracious David-West]], a [[serial killer]] who killed 15 women in [[Port Harcourt]], [[Rivers State]], between July and September 2019, is sentenced [[capital punishment|to death]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-54433201 (BBC News)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 Czech Senate election]]
**The second round to [[Elections in the Czech Republic|elect]] a third of the [[Czech Republic]]'s [[Senate of the Czech Republic|Senate]] takes place. The first round indicated an electoral victory for [[Prime Minister of the Czech Republic|Prime Minister]] [[Andrej Babiš]]' party [[ANO 2011]]. [https://www.foreignbrief.com/daily-news/czech-senate-to-start-second-round-of-elections/ (Foreign Brief)]
*[[2020 Nobel Peace Prize]]
**The [[Nobel Peace Prize]] is awarded to the [[United Nations]] [[World Food Programme]] "for its efforts to combat hunger, for its contribution to bettering conditions for peace in conflict-affected areas and for acting as a driving force in efforts to prevent the use of hunger as a weapon of war and conflict." [https://edition.cnn.com/europe/live-news/nobel-peace-prize-2020-scli-intl/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Cyprus dispute]]
**The self-declared [[Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus]] re-opens [[Varosha, Famagusta]], to the public. The area was [[ghost town|abandoned]] in 1974 during the [[Turkish invasion of Cyprus]], and access is forbidden under international law imposed by the [[United Nations Buffer Zone in Cyprus]]. [[Russia]] condemns the decision, calling it "unacceptable", and [[Cyprus]] has requested the [[United Nations]] intervene to stop the re-opening. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/oct/09/terrible-day-anger-as-pictures-show-varosha-beach-in-cyprus-opening-after-46-years (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2020 United States presidential debates]]
**The [[Commission on Presidential Debates]] formally cancels the second [[United States presidential debates|presidential debate]] of the [[2020 United States presidential election|2020 election]], scheduled for October 15 between Donald Trump and [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]] nominee [[Joe Biden]]. It is the first time in [[U.S. history]] that a presidential debate has been cancelled. An alternative "virtual debate" was proposed due to health concerns after Trump tested positive for [[COVID-19]], but was turned down by Trump. [https://edition.cnn.com/2020/10/09/politics/second-presidential-debate-canceled/index.html (CNN)]
*[[2020 Kyrgyzstani protests]]
**[[President of Kyrgyzstan|President]] [[Sooronbay Jeenbekov]] declares a [[state of emergency]] in the capital [[Bishkek]] and deploys the [[Armed Forces of Kyrgyzstan|country's armed forces]] across the city following serious political unrest that came after the now-overturned [[October 2020 Kyrgyz parliamentary election|2020 elections]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2020/10/09/europe/kyrgyzstan-troops-state-emergency-intl/index.html (CNN)]
**Jeenbekov says that he is ready to resign once a [[Government of Kyrgyzstan|new cabinet]] is approved. [https://www.ft.com/content/db1e81f1-a330-4fb0-8eca-3898cd3c355b (''Financial Times'')] [http://www.nagalandpost.com/ready-to-resign-after-cabinet-s-approval-kyrgyz-president/223041.html (''Nagaland Post'')] 

;Science and technology 
*[[Internet censorship in Pakistan]], [[Censorship of TikTok]]
**[[Pakistan]] announces that it would ban Chinese app [[TikTok]] after it did not take down "immoral and indecent" content on the platform. The government kept the door open for a return of TikTok, saying "it is open for engagement" and would review its decision if TikTok develops a mechanism to moderate this content. [https://apnews.com/article/media-china-social-media-archive-pakistan-d507b6a7a7155534ff8082c8fe42bd74 (AP)]

;Sports
*[[2020 Paris–Roubaix]]
**In road cycling, the organizers cancel the postponed 2020 edition of [[Paris–Roubaix]], which was originally to be held in April, but then postponed to October 25, due to new restrictions that were announced in [[Lille]] to combat the [[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]. [https://www.skysports.com/more-sports/cycling/news/15264/12099873/paris-roubaix-race-cancelled-for-2020-due-to-new-coronavirus-restrictions-in-lille-area (Sky Sports)]
